title: CommentSubmission
description: What a browser may send to the site Worker's comment endpoints (RFC-0007): `POST /__cloudhal/comments` (a comment) and `POST /__cloudhal/comments/report` (a report). Forms post application/x-www-form-urlencoded and the comments module posts JSON; the server builds this object from either (the endpoint sets `kind`, the server sets `schemaVersion`) and checks it with the precompiled validator before anything else reads it. Everything in it is untrusted. It is loose where the server normalises (it trims, NFC-normalises and re-checks text against the stored Comment contract) and strict where a browser has no business sending something: there is no field for a status, a site, an author kind, a label, an IP address or anything the server derives itself.

oneOf.title: CommentPostSubmission
oneOf.description: A new comment or a reply.

nodeId.description: The entry commented on. The server accepts it only for a published entry with an open thread, and works out the page to return to itself.

parentId.description: The comment replied to; it must be approved and in the same thread. The server decides `parentId`/`inReplyToId` of the stored comment.

name.description: The display name as typed (the form says it is shown publicly).

email.description: Optional and never shown. Kept only for moderation, erasure and export requests (v1.1: reply notifications after double opt-in).

body.description: The comment as typed; the server trims and normalises it, then requires 2 to 5,000 characters.

oneOf.title: CommentReportSubmission
oneOf.description: A reader's notice that a comment breaks the site's rules or the law (EU DSA Art. 16). A report never hides anything by itself: it puts the comment in front of a person.

details.description: Why, as typed; at most 1,000 characters after normalising.

email.description: Optional, never shown: where the site may answer the notice.

SubmissionChallenge.description: The signed proof-of-work challenge from `GET /__cloudhal/comments/challenge`, as issued (base64url segments joined by dots).

SubmissionSolution.description: The counter that solves the challenge, in decimal.

SubmissionTurnstileToken.description: Cloudflare Turnstile's response token, when the site turned Turnstile on.

SubmissionHoneypot.description: A field people never see. The schema accepts any short value so that a filled honeypot gets the same answer as a real submission ("held for moderation") and nothing is stored.
